title: IG Metall workers hold warning strike and march in Neckarsulm

tea.why: Workers are protesting for higher wages and expressing concern over the potential closure of the Audi plant in Neckarsulm.
tea.want: The union demands a five percent wage increase and the long-term security of jobs at the Audi and KS sites.
tea.changed: Nov 6: Approximately 6,500 workers participated in the warning strike and march through the industrial area.

summary: On November 6, 2026, employees at the Audi plant and the KS Pistons and KS AluTech facilities in Neckarsulm participated in a warning strike and protest march. Organised by the IG Metall union, the action involved two separate demonstration marches that converged for a rally in the Hafenstraße industrial area. Participants used drums and fireworks to voice their demands for a five percent wage increase and job security amidst concerns regarding the future of the Audi production site. The protest follows ongoing collective bargaining negotiations in the metal and electrical industry. An Audi spokesperson described the strike as part of the standard tariff round. While the employer side has offered a one-time payment and a 1.3 percent wage increase for 2028, workers highlighted the preservation of their plant as their primary concern.
demands: Preservation of the Audi Neckarsulm plant
response: An Audi spokesperson stated that the warning strike is part of the current collective bargaining round, which involves employer associations and Südwestmetall.

crowd.text: The IG Metall union reported that approximately 6,500 people participated in the warning strike.

updates.text: Workers from Audi and the KS site held a warning strike and march in Neckarsulm to demand higher wages and job security.
